messages:
nina_k: Hi all - first day! I accepted the org invite and can view repos in the web UI, but my `git push` over SSH fails with permission denied. Clone works via HTTPS though. Anyone seen this? :thinking:
onboarding-bot: Welcome @nina_k! Common SSH issues: key tied to another account, wrong SSH key loaded, or commit email not matching. @it-support can you help?
it-support: Hey Nina - can you paste the exact error and the output of `ssh -T git@github.com` and `git remote -v`? Also which SSH key are you using (id_rsa, id_ed25519)?
nina_k: Error: "Permission denied (publickey). fatal: Could not read from remote repository."
ssh -T output: "git@github.com: Permission denied (publickey)."
git remote -v: "origin git@github.com:redwood-inference/cli.git (fetch)
origin git@github.com:redwood-inference/cli.git (push)"
I'm using `~/.ssh/id_rsa` (old key).
it-support: That usually means your public key isn't registered on the GH account you're SSO-ing with. Can you check https://github.com/settings/keys in the browser after SSO? Also run `ssh-add -l` to see which key agent is offering.
nina_k: `ssh-add -l` shows the key fingerprint and comment "nina.personal@gmail.com". I think this key is attached to my personal GH account.
luca: If the SSH key's comment/email points at your personal account, GitHub will match it there. Two options: add a new work SSH key and upload to your work account, or remove that key from personal account. We usually prefer separate keys for work.
security: Quick note: if you add a new key, mark it as a work key and keep your personal keys separate. Don't share private keys.
it-support: Steps: 1) `ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "nina@redwood.com" -f ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_redwood` 2) `cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_redwood.pub` -> paste to https://github.com/settings/keys on your work account after SSO. 3) Add to ssh-agent: `ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_redwood`. 4) Update `~/.ssh/config` with a Host alias to force the right key: ``Host github.com
  HostName github.com
  User git
  IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_redwood``
nina_k: Did the new key flow, added it in after SSO. `ssh -T git@github.com` now returns "Hi nina_k! You've successfully authenticated..." But push still 403 when I try to push a branch. The push error: "remote: Permission to redwood-inference/cli.git denied to nina.personal. fatal: unable to access 'https://github.com/redwood-inference/cli.git/': The requested URL returned error: 403"
git-bot: Automated: pushes via HTTPS may use cached credentials (PAT) tied to a different GH account. If you want to use SSH, ensure remote uses `git@github.com:...` not `https://` and clear credential helpers for HTTPS.
it-support: Looks like your remote is mixed or you previously pushed with HTTPS + PAT for personal account. Run `git remote set-url origin git@github.com:redwood-inference/cli.git` to force SSH remote and try push. Also clear cached HTTPS creds: mac `git credential-osxkeychain erase` or `git credential-manager-core erase` on Windows.
nina_k: Switched to SSH remote and pushed successfully! Thanks everyone :tada:
luca: Welcome to the team @nina_k — added you to team cli-maintainers. If you need infra access, ping @it-support.
security: Confirmed new SSH key is in org audit. All good.
onboarding-bot: Welcome aboard @nina_k! If you hit anything else with repo perms, post here or open an IT ticket.
